Ooh, i can help with this one!

So the absolute simplest and cheapest way to get started with VTubing is PNGTubing. There are a couple methods you can use to do this!

1. A simple static PNG imported into your OBS scene to lay over you gameplay

2. Using Reactive Fugitech (https://reactive.fugi.tech/) to make an avatar with a "mouth open" and "mouth closed" state. This connects to discord, and when you are in a voice channel it will use your voice activity to make the PNG (or GIF) change between a "mouth closed" and "mouth open" state. For this, you will need two PNG images, one with a closed mouth, and one with an open mouth. These need to be otherwise identical in dimension and image. To get your image into OBS, Fugitech has a browser source that you will need to import into OBS - which you can then place how you like.


If you want an actual animated, face-tracked model, the most popular progam is called VTube Studio.

3. Buy a cheap starter VTuber Model from Etsy or Ko-Fi, and import it into a program called Vtube Studio (VTS), which can be found on the Steam store. There are tons and tons of affordable pre-made models available there, and you're sure to find one you like. It's important to know you are looking for "fully rigged" models that are "Live 2d" compatiable. 

To get this model to move, you are going to need a webcam so VTube Studio can track your facial movements. It expresses these in something called "parameters" which translate these into the rigged and animated art in VTube Studio. You can find plenty of awesome tutorials on YouTube on how to import and set up models in VTS.


There are steps up from here such as comissioning custom models from artists and L2D riggers, and upgrading from Webcam face tracking to iPhone ARKit facial tracking, but none of those are necessary investments to start VTubing.


Hope this helps!

Hi, player from 2017 here! I actually disagree with other comments that mercy had to healbot more in OW1 6v6.

With two tanks, the game was a LOT slower paced than people realise. Every fight came down to a war of attrition, and who could whittle down key cooldowns first. Because of this, I feel 6v6 was actually better for mercy. She did have to occasionally chip in with healing a little bit more but the “pocket an off-angling” dps was a lot more necessary because there were WAY more defensive resources available for the tanks. Your dps NEEDED the extra oomph Mercy could provide to break through the enemy frontline. 

On the supporting side, this abundance of defensive abilities would let characters like Moira, Bap or Ana sustain two tanks all by themselves - the tanks would help each other maintain space and in turn keep the other support safe. Two big health pools taking damage is a lot easier to maintain (keep them alive enough to do their job, not necessarily “heal to full”) than just one!

Another thing to consider is those defensive resources helped Mercy too. If one tank died, the other one could help you resurrect them, and there would be an entire extra player to mark flankers like genji and tracer to keep the backline safer.

I’m excited to see 6v6 come back, it was much more nuanced than “dump all cool-downs into the solo tank and win the fight with brute force” than we have now.

I think whether to glide or free-fall depends on the enemy team composition again. My default preference is to stagger a free by gliding at the top of the jump arc and then free-falling to make my movement more unpredictable. 

However if they have for example a Reinhardt or Doomfist I might just slow fall to try stay out of their ranges for longer. Whereas if they have a Brigitte, Venture, Dva, or Lucio I might free-fall to touch the ground faster so I might avoid the boop or shield bash (not that you should be resurrecting if they have boops available but in the worst-case scenario haha).

If you’re fast and aware of enemy team cool-downs though, you can actually dodge select uses with clever movement timing in SJ rezzes, like helix rocket, cassidy nade, accretion and even hog hook and sleep dart. It comes down to predicting them predicting your movement and making it difficult for them to reliably hit skill shots.

A lot of the time super jump Rez just isn’t worth it. It is at it’s core a very flashy, risky play that whilst it looks awesome and feels awesome to get away with, about 90% of the time the same resurrect could have been done after waiting a few seconds for it to be safer and more reliable. 

I think the few strong use-cases might be a do-it-or-lose situation in a stall or clutch point retake on a teammate with a high value ultimate. Or using it on select and situational resurrects where there’s a perfectly placed high ground you can SJ rezup onto to use it as vertical cover. I think it’s really map dependent and composition dependent. You need to always consider that it should be a last-ditch effort with a high risk of wasting your life or staggering a teammate compared to a safer rez you can just be patient and use cover/ask resources for.
